RINGSPEC — the spectrum of a ring, in integers
=============================================

  units:   4
  weights: 1 1 1 1 
  topology: pure cycle — every junction one clean bond

  char poly det(λI − A) = λ^4 + -4λ^2

  Σλ² = tr(A²) = 8   (= 2·Σwᵢ² = 2·4)  ✓
  spectrum symmetric under λ ↦ -λ: YES — every odd coefficient vanishes
  ⟹ the top eigenvalue is paired with its negative, so |λ₂| = ρ
  ⟹ SPECTRAL GAP = 0 exactly — no privileged mode

  even ring — bipartite, so gap 0 whatever the weights.
  Bipartite means the units fall into two classes and every bond runs
  between them. A ring alternates because something mediates on both
  sides of what it mediates — which is also why the count is even. One
  fact, two readings. Compare gap within a parity; across parities the
  gap is fixed before any weight is read, so compare strain instead.
  zero eigenvalues: 2 (λ^2 divides the polynomial)
  ⟹ the spectrum is {0 ×2, ±ρ} with ρ² = Σλ²/2 = 4 EXACTLY

  Every line above is an integer identity. A ring reported as ρ=3.1623
  has to be believed; one reported as ρ²=10 can be checked.
